units.translation: 1-5a. Come now, Erato: They say that Erato invented dancing. Reasonably, then, Apollonius says that Erato has been allotted the rites of Aphrodite, I mean the nuptial rites; for dancing also attends marriages. In the works attributed to Musaeus (2 B 15 Diels-Kranz) two births of the Muses are recorded: the elder ones in the time of Cronus, and the younger ones from Zeus and Mnemosyne.

b. Come now, Erato: It is said that of the Muses, Clio invented history, Thalia agriculture and the study of plants, Euterpe learning, Terpsichore play, Erato dancing, Polymnia the lyre, Melpomene song, Urania astronomy, and Calliope poetry.

c. It is especially questioned why he invokes the Muse, having invoked Apollo in Book 1. Some say that Erato is handed down in the Orphic poems (fg 39 Kern) as the inventor of dancing; since, then, he is about to narrate the marriage of Medea, for this reason he invokes the Muse who is the inventor of the dancing that belongs to marriage. Others say that the Muses are patronesses of festivities; therefore the Muse will not be alien to the marriage. That the Muses are patronesses of festivities is shown in the Orphic poems (fg 38 Kern): 'Nor do mortals forget the Muses; for they are queens, to whom dance and lovely festivities are a care.' Rhianus in Book 1 of the Eliaca says that it makes no difference if one invokes one of the Muses; for through one he signifies all. He speaks thus (fg III 3 Meineke Anal. Alex. 1843, 202): 'All hear, whenever you utter the name of one.'
